newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to meet wheat needs, export maize in '97.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to meet wheat needs, export maize in '97.

text.p: Croatia will be self-sufficient in wheat this year and will have an estimated 470,000-tonne maize surplus for export, Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic said on Monday.

Croatian farmers have sown 250,000 hectares to wheat and expect to harvest around 780,000 tonnes, which would compare with estimated domestic demand of 650-720,000, Dominikovic told a news conference.
Maize was sown on some 400-420,000 ha and should yield 2-2.1 million tonnes, leaving some 470,000 for export.
Increased cereals output is expected to reduce bread prices by some 20 percent this year, Dominikovic said.
The country will meet its sugar beet needs and some 68 percent of its requirements for sunflower, rapeseed and soybeans, he added.
The ministry plans to boost domestic production of key farming products in the next three years and has prepared 570 million kuna for subsidies in 1997.
"Croatia is importing a lot of food, and we need to increase sowings, revive cattle breeding and find additional favourable funds for our farmers," Dominikovic said.
The ministry plans to increase livestock numbers, heavily depleted during the four-year war, by some 145,000 cattle in the next three years in order to meet domestic demand for milk and meat.
"We should be able to become self-sufficient in milk in 1998 or 1999 at the latest," Dominikovic said.
Croatia imports 130,000 cattle and 417,000 pigs a year to meet its demand for meat.
Some 220,000 hectares of arable land are idle, Dominikovic said, adding that these areas should be brought back into production in the next three years.
